title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1966-09-16
source: SBD>MR>?>LP>ZoomH4>WaveLab 5.0>FLAC24</br>Linn LP12 turntable, SME III tonearm, Benz ACE H2 Cartridge, Rotel RC 1082 preamp</br>Transfer by indidarkstar

ai_review.summary: A clean, well‑balanced vinyl rip captures an early‑’66 show bursting with high energy – standout versions of “I Know You Rider,” “Midnight Hour,” “Lindy” and a brilliant “All Over Now, Baby Blue.”
ai_review.review: The recording is a very clean transfer from the original Avalon vinyl source, with virtually no surface noise and balanced channel separation despite slightly low levels. The performance itself is full‑throttle early Dead – Jerry’s jazzy, high‑speed solos blaze on “I Know You Rider” and “Midnight Hour,” Bob’s youthful rhythm drives a playful “Lindy,” and the band’s collective joy lifts every song.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise both the musical performance (energy, standout solos) and the technical fidelity of the vinyl rip; averaged star scores are high and comments are consistent.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean vinyl rip with virtually no surface noise, good channel separation, slightly low overall levels but balanced mix; matches original pitch and is clearer than other releases.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑career set that moves from bluesy jams to upbeat folk‑rock numbers, maintaining a playful momentum and tight transitions throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for blazing, jazz‑inflected solos, high‑speed bluegrass runs and an “on fire” tone on several tracks.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for youthful rhythm guitar work (Weir appears to be around 18) that adds fun and drive, especially on “Stealin'.”
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard parts described as great, adding sophisticated texture and supporting the band’s high‑energy vibe.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers highlighted for tight, dynamic interplay with Jerry and Pig, creating memorable ad‑libs and driving the overall excitement.
